page: Amazon Web Services m5d.24xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz across 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs on an x86_64 instruction set. The system includes 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Attached to the instance are 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial aggregate multi-threaded execution power, supported by strong results in stress-ng multi-core testing (81,319.36), PassMark CPU score (55,443.45), and extended instruction processing (73,965.40). The instance delivers high caching and uncached memory bandwidth alongside strong I/O capabilities, achieving 74.41 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 43.63 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, as demonstrated by weak single-threaded performance in stress-ng (1380.89) and Geekbench (1147.0), as well as poor tokens-per-second rates during LLM text generation tasks.

Cost efficiency is driven by high-density horizontal compute and extensive bundled NVMe storage. Systems that can saturate parallel threads and leverage local scratch capacity maximize value, whereas single-threaded bottlenecks or workloads demanding modern GPU acceleration will experience suboptimal hardware efficiency.

AWS m5d.24xlarge is well suited for highly parallelized multi-threaded tasks, distributed data processing, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, large-scale build farms, and high-throughput static web serving fleets requiring local temporary storage.
